newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM, RENAULT CLASH AGAIN OVER CAR PLANT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM, RENAULT CLASH AGAIN OVER CAR PLANT.

text.p: Belgian authorities and France's Renault are at loggerheads again, this time over the terms the car maker's Vilvoorde factory would be sold to a potential new investor, Belgian officials said on Wednesday.

Talks over whether a buyer would have to pay a market or symbolic price for the site have broken down and would resume after the summer, Koen De Backer, an advisor to Flanders Economics Minister Eric Van Rompuy, told Reuters.
Van Rompuy told VTM television on Tuesday the French car maker had reneged on a promise of favourable terms for any new investor after an agreed upon three-year grace period.
Renault union FGTB said in a statement on Wednesday that Renault "had always promised verbally to sell the grounds, buildings and installations for a nominal franc to an eventual buyer."

De Backer said, however, under Renault's latest proposal, which has been refused by Van Rompuy, "if someone who had invested in the second year, partially attracted by the cheap price, and later wanted to expand his operations, he would have to pay the full market price."
The Flemish government fears such a proposal would scare away potential investors.
Talks between the two sides are due to resume on August 25.
